en: The Praise and Aspiration Prayer of Vajrayoginī, composed by the accomplished master Virūpāda.
Om, homage to the glorious Vajrayoginī!
Homage to the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha; homage to the Gurus, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas; homage to Locanā and the other ten Vajravilāsinīs.
Homage to the ten heroic wrathful deities, Yamāntaka and the rest, together with their consorts.
*Oṃ o ā hūṃ*—these are the body, speech, and mind, the sense faculties and consciousnesses;
speech, mind, and mental consciousness.
The supernormal knowledge of knowing the minds of others and the supernormal knowledge of entering other bodies; in the lotuses situated at the navel is a red solar mandala. || 1 ||
The Dharmodayā, in the center of the lotus, has a form as red as vermilion;
it is indeed three-peaked or triangular, and is endowed with four seats.
The syllable *hrīṃ* is proclaimed to be its yellow-colored center;
born from that, the yellow-colored Avadhūtī herself abides there. (3)
In the *lalanā* she is Suśyāmā, and in the *rasanā* she is Gaurikā;
in the center, she is named Pratyālīḍhapadā, yellow and beautiful.
Established in the three paths, the Goddess is the Vajrayoginī of the three bodies;
she alone, by name, is the Ḍākinī of all the perfectly awakened ones.
Possessing a divine form throughout the three worlds and fulfilling all hopes,
she held her own head, which she had cut off with her own sword, in her left hand.
To her right stands the knife (kartī), which cuts through the suffering of the world;
to her left stands the dark-complexioned one named Varavarṇinī.
In her left hand she holds a skull-bowl, and a flaying knife is positioned in her right;
and indeed, in the right [hand] stands the yellow Vajravairocanī.
Holding a knife in her right hand and bearing a skull-cup in her left,
the goddess stands in the pratyālīḍha posture and is especially naked.
Her two hands and her two feet are likewise positioned in reverse;
she is the mother of the Buddhas, the central one, possessing the form of a perfectly enlightened Buddha.
She is eternally inexhaustible and auspicious, the destroyer of both death and birth;
her essential nature consists of the Dharmakāya, Sambhogakāya, Nirmāṇakāya, and Mahāsukha. (11)
May this Goddess always shine like the moon in the three worlds;
from Kabandha and Avadhūtī, she shall enter her own mouths with blood.
Emerging from the lalanā and rasanā channels and likewise reaching the head,
she drinks [the essence] in a form red with compassion for the sake of all-pervading peace.
Having beheld the suffering of the worlds, she is the destroyer of the four Māras; cutting away dejection and the like, she cuts through all of that indeed.
O Mother of the Victors, you have indeed been praised; be well-pleased in this ocean of existence, so that I may become capable of accomplishing my own welfare and the welfare of others. 15.
Therefore, O Goddess, you must bestow grace upon me;
for I am but a child, ignorant in nature due to the defects of body, speech, and mind. (16)
"I do not know devotion to the guru, nor especially devotion to You; O Sovereign of the World, perceive this and let Your grace be bestowed upon me. (17)
By your grace, bring about the equilibrium of my body, speech, and mind, so that I may abandon cyclic existence and no longer enter the six realms of rebirth. (18)
And how my body may become like a diamond until I am liberated, and how I may be abandoned by all Māras—may my body be thus. (19)
Through this play, one shall partake in accomplishments; being free from obstacles, one shall possess all perfections.
There shall be success in all spiritual practices, and the body itself shall be free from old age and death.
The terrifier of all Māras, the fulfiller of all hopes—grant me supreme accomplishment, having abandoned coming and going. (21)
O Goddess, let the mind, together with the five sense faculties, be dissolved;
then the true bliss of the life, youth, and health of Vajrasattva shall be accomplished. 22.
Through your grace, the Mahāmudrā may arise for everyone—whether gods, asuras, or humans—wherever they may dwell;
and may they all be happy and attain the fruit of Buddhahood. || 23 ||
In the *Śrīguhyasamayatantro*, the praise and aspiration prayer to Trikāyavajrayoginī is complete.
This work is the composition of the accomplished master, the venerable Virūpāda.
